requirement_text.REQ-214: Closes ISS-0411/GH#807 (queue task 411): Letflow.Engine never dispatches :SERVICE_TASK nodes. dispatch_node/4 (lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex:334-339) hits its generic {:error, {:node_type_not_yet_implemented, :SERVICE_TASK, node_id}} catch-all for every SERVICE_TASK node -- the one Graph.node_type() variant that reaches it. REQ-056 (done, S3) already shipped the pure logic this requirement wires up: Letflow.Engine.ServiceTask's parse_config_from_node_attributes/1, classify_failure_kind/1, is_retriable_failure/1, decide_failure/3, compute_service_task_backoff_ms/3, build_idempotency_key/4, build_service_task_give_up_error_attrs/1, build_empty_url_error_attrs/1 -- see lib/letflow/design/service_task.md, which deliberately left the transport, the service_catalog lookup, and the dispatch-orchestration loop itself out of scope (its own §1 table). REQ-177 (done, S6) separately wired the give-up outcome into Letflow.Dlq.enqueue/2. Both requirements' own design docs name this exact remaining gap; ISS-0411 is that gap surfacing as a real platform defect (discovered via REQ-208's Meridian committee-vote/disbursement paths sitting behind undispatchable SERVICE_TASK nodes) rather than new-invented scope. THIS REQUIREMENT IS THE CORE: the HTTP transport, the dispatch decision loop, and its supervised process -- mirroring REQ-186's own split (Letflow.Scheduler's core/poller, no route/engine wiring in that requirement) rather than REQ-187's engine-wiring half, which is REQ-215. SCOPE: 1. A concrete transport_fun() implementation (REQ-056 design §3.4) using :httpc.request/4 -- already this codebase's own established outbound-HTTP mechanism (REQ-183's Letflow.Webhooks.dispatch_http/3, :inets/:ssl already started per mix.exs's own comment at that call site) -- rather than adding a new HTTP client library dependency. No new decision record is needed: :httpc is already the platform's one outbound-HTTP mechanism, used identically for the same tenant-authored-URL threat model REQ-183/REQ-204 already solved. 2. SECURITY (BLOCKER, INV-9): every dispatch call, for BOTH route_kind values, MUST call Letflow.Webhooks.UrlValidator.validate/2 (lib/letflow/webhooks/url_validator.ex, REQ-204) against the fully rendered URL immediately before the :httpc.request/4 call -- identical defence-in-depth placement to Letflow.Webhooks.dispatch_http/3,4 (lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:373-392). A blocked URL returns the same {:error, :target_url_not_allowed} shape UrlValidator already defines; the caller (REQ-215) routes it through ServiceTask.build_service_task_give_up_error_attrs/1's :request_build_error-shaped give-up path (no retry -- an SSRF-blocked URL is deterministic, retrying cannot succeed, exactly like :request_build_error's own existing rationale in service_task.md §5.3). SERVICE_TASK's own url_template is tenant-authored graph-node attribute data (definition-author-controlled, same trust boundary webhook target_url has) -- this is a real SSRF surface, not a speculative one, and SECURITY-REVIEWER is a hard gate on this requirement for exactly that reason. 3. route_kind: :catalog_service dispatch: since S6's service_catalog (src/repository/service_catalog.zig) is NOT built (no table, no lookup module exists anywhere in lib/), this requirement's catalog_lookup_fun() implementation (REQ-056 design §3.5) returns {:error, :not_registered} unconditionally for every service_id -- stated explicitly in the moduledoc as a real, current limitation (route_kind: :catalog_service dispatch attempts). :not_registered routes through the same give-up path as an SSRF block (deterministic, no retry). Building the real catalog is explicitly NOT this requirement -- named as a future requirement, not silently deferred unremarked. 4. The dispatch-orchestration process: a new context module, Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher, plus a new supervised poller process, Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller, added to Letflow.Application's supervision tree (lib/letflow/application.ex) alongside the existing Letflow.Scheduler.Poller entry -- same architecture, NOT the same process (SERVICE_TASK dispatch and TIMER firing are independent concerns with independent poll cadences and independent per-tenant claim queries; do not overload Letflow.Scheduler.Poller with a second responsibility). Mirrors Letflow.Scheduler's own design exactly (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex, lib/letflow/design/req185-scheduler-firing-architecture.md, lib/letflow/design/req186-scheduler-core.md): supervised GenServer ticker (no Oban, matching this codebase's own already-decided no-background-job-library posture), FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim per tenant schema, one Repo.transaction/1 per claimed dispatch attempt, no startup-sweep lock. A parked SERVICE_TASK token needs its own durable "pending dispatch" record to poll against -- reuse the shape decision REQ-186 already made for exactly this problem (a `service_task_dispatches` table analogous to `timers`, holding instance_id, token_id, node_id, config snapshot, attempt_index, next_attempt_at, status) rather than inventing a different persistence shape; this requirement owns that table's migration and schema module. 5. On each poll claim: call the config's transport_fun() (step 1), classify the raw outcome via REQ-056's classify_failure_kind/1, decide via decide_failure/3 using the row's own attempt_index and the config's retry_limit. :retry re-schedules next_attempt_at using compute_service_task_backoff_ms/3 and increments attempt_index in the same transaction (no sleep -- the poller's own poll interval is the wait mechanism, exactly like Letflow.Scheduler never sleeping inside fire_timer/2). :give_up (either exhausted retries or an immediately non-retriable kind) computes build_service_task_give_up_error_attrs/1's attrs and returns them to REQ-215's caller -- THIS module does not call Letflow.Engine.set_instance_error/2 itself (that call site belongs to REQ-215's engine-wiring layer, per REQ-056 design §6's own routing statement: "a future dispatch-orchestration caller... is required to invoke" set_instance_error/2, not this module doing it directly, keeping Letflow.Engine.* as the sole caller of its own standalone_error_attrs()-consuming functions). 6. A successful (2xx, JSON-object body) dispatch: this module returns the decoded body to REQ-215's caller for REQ-049's VariableMerge and token advancement -- again, this module does not call Letflow.Engine functions itself; it returns a typed outcome (:advance, decoded_body) | (:give_up, standalone_error_attrs()) | :retry_scheduled, and REQ-215 supplies the actual Engine call sites, matching the same layering Letflow.Scheduler/Letflow.Engine.advance_after_timer_fired/3 already established (poller module calls into Letflow.Engine, not the reverse). NOT IN THIS REQUIREMENT, AND WHY: (a) dispatch_node/4's own :SERVICE_TASK dispatch clause and the activation-time async-park write (the transition.ex/engine.ex wiring analogous to REQ-187's role for TIMER) -- REQ-215, so this requirement's own module can be built and unit-tested (transport_fun, classification, claim/poll loop) against synthetic parked-dispatch rows before the Engine can ever produce a real one. (b) The real service_catalog (S6, still unbuilt) -- step 3 above states the stub explicitly rather than building it. (c) HTTP request cancellation/abort on instance cancellation (REQ-187's own description already named this as REQ-056's deferred "HTTP-abort half" and explicitly excluded it from REQ-187's own scope) -- still deferred; this requirement's poller simply lets an already-dispatched :httpc.request/4 call complete or time out per-request (the config's own timeout_ms), it does not add a new cross-request cancellation mechanism. A row belonging to a since-cancelled/completed instance is skipped at claim time (same SCH-03-style check REQ-187 already established for timers) rather than aborted mid-flight. (d) No change to lib/letflow/engine/service_task.ex itself (REQ-056's pure functions) beyond what step 1-3 above requires wiring against -- no re-litigating its already-shipped classification/backoff/decision algorithms.
